questions.q: The failure classifier fires a recovery action only when:
options: Confidence exceeds 70% within the 20-second vote window
Any single signal arrives
The DBA clicks approve in PagerDuty
Heartbeat age exceeds 15 seconds all by itself
questions.explain: The 70% threshold is a hard gate: below it the system escalates to a human via PagerDuty while continuing to collect signals; above it the recovery pipeline fires autonomously.

questions.q: What ADE principle governs autonomous actions that would cause data loss?
options: Data loss is acceptable for lagging async replicas
Async replicas may be promoted silently within the RPO
Autonomous systems need explicit permission to cause data loss (e.g. a data_loss_authorized flag) — it is never implicit by default
The circuit breaker automatically authorizes it
questions.explain: Every path that would exceed RPO without pre-authorization terminates in human escalation; data_loss_authorized may be true in dev/staging but never silently in production.

questions.q: Autonomous point-in-time recovery restores to which point relative to corruption detection?
options: The latest log backup
5 minutes before the corruption detection timestamp, to avoid restoring already-corrupt data
The exact detection timestamp
One hour after detection, to be safe
questions.explain: The PITR selection subtracts a 5-minute safety margin from the detection timestamp, then chains the most recent full backup, differential, and logs with STOPAT.

questions.q: What opens the DR circuit breaker, and what happens while it is open?
options: One failure opens it for 1 minute
It opens only on an explicit human command
Five consecutive successes open it
Three failed recovery attempts within the 10-minute window open it for 5 minutes; all autonomous actions are blocked and a human is paged
questions.explain: The breaker prevents recovery spirals (repeated failed promotions); after 5 minutes it goes half-open for one probe action, closing again only on success.

questions.q: When the decision engine classifies the failure as split-brain, what is the first action?
options: Escalate to a human immediately
Fence the old primary before anything else
Promote the sync replica
Restore from backup
questions.explain: Split-brain demands fencing first: promoting a replica while the original primary still accepts writes produces dual primaries, so the old primary is shot in the head (STONITH) before promotion.
